name: Jan van Nassau to Willem van Oranje, Dillenburg, 21 Nov 1573 (WVO 5549): body runs 1-61 in the 'verendertte' key
ciphertext_source: KHA A 11/XIV A/5-18 (images/05549_p1-6.jpg, WVO PDF 150 dpi), image-checked against Groen van Prinsterer, Archives 1re serie Supplement, Lettre 45, pp.140-148 (groen/groen_5549.tsv; J5I, 24 Sept 2026): runs 1-61 = 537 numerals + 55 clear fragments (grade 'both' 590, 'image' 2, 'M' 1); the postscript stretch PS1-PS26 (226 tokens, pp.4-5) is a separate file, ciphertext_5549_ps.tsv, already read under Lodewijk's 1574 table (J5S, AX-MERGE).
alphabet: numerals 1-345 (134 distinct in the body; 24 pct above 99), roman numerals as drawn, clear German fragments inside runs

constraints.body_key: the letter's own opening says the body is in the 'verendertte Instruction oder Ciffer' just received from Willem; its postscript says the writer went back to 'die alte Ciffer' to the end -- and that final stretch reads under Lodewijk's 1574 table (J5S). The body does NOT read under that table, nor under key_1572 (J5S, J6, J7); no sibling letter in the body's key was found among 5550, 5552, 5557, 5575, 5797, 5204, 5205, 5207-5209, 5213, 5214, 5210, 5812, 5810 (J6, R4-C, WC-NASSAU-FIT, FIT2).
constraints.control_backed_negative: J7 (24 Sept 2026): nomenclator_anneal.py --lang de, 16 x 400k, control (same run pattern, 539 tokens, 113 types) read only 10.9 pct of tokens -- the design is beyond that method at this length.

cheap_tests: known-answer step on the postscript stretch: key_full vs Groen's clear print, key and transcription scored separately (likely8/run.py step 1)
key_1572, key_5549 and key_full applied to the 537 body groups vs 20 value-shuffled copies of each key (likely8/run.py step 2)

judge.note: 2 Oct 2026, LIKELY-8: the de language corpus (tools/data/de16/composed_enhg.txt, 8.5 KB composed) fails the letter's own genuine clear prose (Groen Suppl. pp.140-148: lm median -1.34 vs real_p05 -0.45); a FAIL or PASS from this judge is not a test for this target until a period ENHG corpus replaces it. Use word cover vs value-shuffled keys (likely8/run.py) as the gate meanwhile.

cheap_test_done.test: known answer: postscript under key_full vs Groen clear print (18 lines)
cheap_test_done.verdict: key right; transcription ~92-96% on the postscript

cheap_test_done.test: body (537 groups) under key_1572 / key_5549 / key_full vs 20 value-shuffled copies of each
cheap_test_done.control: shuffle cover mean 0.195 / 0.114 / 0.200 (max 0.265 / 0.142 / 0.237); instrument control = PS stretch under key_full cover 0.354 vs shuffle max 0.280
cheap_test_done.verdict: negative, control-backed, for all three keys; de16 judge void for this target (genuine Groen prose of the letter scores lm median -1.34 vs real_p05 -0.45)
